chapter: Learning the trombone and jam sessions
title: How trombonists played then and hearing Arthur Pryor
summary: Trombonists then only slid; hearing bandmaster Arthur Pryor's command made him want to play differently.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: But, you know, back in those days when I came along, it isn't like today where kids, they learn about tone -- intonation and all this before they even get the instruments they learn. There was no road to go on. We had to make our own road for the kids, you know, today, back there in those days. Really because all a trombone player did back then was -- (imitates a trombone). That's the only way they played. They didn't know any other way to play.

In fact, the first trombone player I ever heard in my life that didn't play like that was a guy called I think it was Arthur Prior. He was a band -- it wasn't a jazz band -- he was a band master, you know. And he played all these intricate parts in a band. And I said, wow, I sure want to play like that, you know. And I don't want to play all this
(imitates a trombone) on the thing. You know, I wanted to really play some nice things like I heard this guy play.

And I started working more on playing things like this, and this is what made me pick up in jazz before I ever got a lesson because I wanted to get around a little bit on the horn and do some different things than what I had been hearing.
